apps.name: romforge
apps.tag: Identify, tidy, enrich and play your ROM collection, from the desk or the sofa.
apps.what: romforge works out exactly what each file is by its fingerprint, gives it the right name and art, and starts it in the right emulator. Scanning only reads. Nothing is moved, renamed or repacked until you've seen the plan and said yes, and every change can be undone.

shots.caption: Fullscreen mode with the Neon Arcade theme

features.title: Identifies every game
features.text: Matches against No-Intro, Redump, TOSEC, MAME and ScummVM by hash, even inside zip, 7z and CHD.

features.title: Tidies your collection
features.text: Renames and repacks into one folder (zip for cartridges, CHD for discs), previewed first, one-click undo.

features.title: Fills in the details
features.text: Box art, screenshots, fanart, logos and release data from free open sources.

features.title: Plays them
features.text: RetroArch or the right standalone emulator: DuckStation, PCSX2, Dolphin, PPSSPP, MAME and more.

features.title: Feels like a console
features.text: Gamepad-driven fullscreen mode for the TV, with community themes.

features.title: Translations and hacks
features.text: Patches a game you own into a translated or hacked copy without touching the original.

install.label: Arch / Manjaro
install.code:
# romforge-bin PKGBUILD from the release
makepkg -si

apps.installNote: Install RetroArch (with a few cores) and any standalone emulators you like. romforge finds them on its own, Flatpaks too.
steps: Open romforge. On first run it offers to make a RomForge folder for your library, games, art, saves and BIOS.
In DATs, download the game lists for your systems.
Scan a folder. Each game shows as verified, candidate or unknown. Nothing changes yet.
Use Search to name what wasn't recognised, and Enrich to fetch art.
Rename & Cleanup shows its plan, then files your verified games. Undo puts everything back.
Press Play, or Fullscreen (F11) and pick up a pad.

apps.name: noti-fi
apps.tag: A notification daemon for KDE Plasma on Wayland, with rules, groups and a control panel.
apps.what: noti-fi (notification fidelity) replaces Plasma's built-in notification service with notifd, built on Quickshell. Rules route each popup into a named group with its own corner of the screen, and the notify command installs it, switches Plasma over and back, and gives you Do Not Disturb, muting, history and a hotkey.

features.title: Groups & rules
features.text: Route popups by app, site, urgency or text, each group in its own corner.

features.title: Safe takeover
features.text: notify takeover --dry-run shows every change; notify restore undoes it.

features.title: Screen-share aware
features.text: Hides notification text while the screen is shared or captured.

features.title: File-job progress
features.text: Dolphin copies, moves and extracts show as popups with live progress.

features.title: Control panel
features.text: Kirigami app for history, appearance, focus modes, groups and rules.

features.title: Self-updating
features.text: notify upgrade checks the release checksum before replacing anything.

install.label: From a release
install.code:
tar xzf noti-fi-*-linux.tar.gz && cd noti-fi-*-linux
./install.sh
notify takeover --dry-run
notify takeover --now

apps.installNote: Needs quickshell, qt6-declarative, kirigami and qqc2-desktop-style at run time. qt6-multimedia is optional.

apps.name: GutCheck
apps.tag: A health check across every GitHub project in a folder.
apps.what: GutCheck scans a folder of repos and grades each one: CI, pull requests, branches, docs, Actions security, dependencies, releases, settings, clutter, tests and AI agent setup. It runs on your existing gh and git login, never handles tokens itself, and also works as a command line and an MCP server so coding agents can use the same checks.

shots.caption: Dashboard: health grades and the repos that need attention
A repo and its findings, each with a fix

features.title: One scan, every repo
features.text: CI, PRs, branches, docs, security, dependencies and releases, graded A to D.

features.title: Fixes you see first
features.text: Every change shows the exact commands before it runs, and only those run.

features.title: Actions security
features.text: Script injection, unpinned actions and loose permissions, read as text.

features.title: Your own rules
features.text: Ignore a finding with a reason, or set a baseline every repo should meet.

features.title: AI agent setup
features.text: Checks CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md size, drift and risky permission rules.

features.title: Local and private
features.text: No account, no server, no telemetry. GitHub data comes through gh.

apps.installNote: Needs gh and git on your PATH, with gh auth login done. Each release ships SHA256SUMS.txt.

apps.name: appOFholding
apps.tag: Keep your AppImages tidy, up to date and sandboxed.
apps.what: appOFholding adds AppImages to your menu, keeps them up to date from GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo or plain links, and can run them in a bubblewrap sandbox. Launch options live in a database, so they survive every update. A Qt/Kirigami app and a CLI share one library.

features.title: Paste a link, get an app
features.text: Picks the right file for your CPU, verifies its checksum and adds it to the menu.

features.title: Import what you have
features.text: Finds loose and already-integrated AppImages and shows a dry-run plan first.

features.title: Updates you can trust
features.text: Checksums, resumable downloads, rollback, and per-app policies.

features.title: Launch options that stick
features.text: Arguments, env, presets like electron-wayland, and hooks.

features.title: Optional sandbox
features.text: Standard or strict bubblewrap, with a private home per app.

features.title: Repeatable setups
features.text: export and apply move your whole setup between machines.

install.label: Quick start
install.code:
appofholding add https://github.com/owner/repo
appofholding import --dry-run
appofholding check && appofholding update

apps.installNote: Building needs Rust 1.89+, Qt 6 with Kirigami, CMake and a C++ compiler. The sandbox needs bubblewrap and xdg-dbus-proxy.

apps.name: Pass Broker
apps.tag: Let AI assistants sign in with your Proton Pass logins without ever seeing them.
apps.what: Pass Broker runs on your PC as a remote MCP server. Assistants such as Claude drive a locked-down browser through redacted tools and only ever get handles, masked snapshots and blacked-out screenshots. Every secret stays on your PC, and every use needs your approval on your desktop.

features.title: Secrets never leave
features.text: Passwords, 2FA codes and your Proton Pass token stay on your PC.

features.title: Approve every use
features.text: A desktop prompt for each sign-in, file unlock or device action.

features.title: Locked-down browser
features.text: Sandboxed Chromium that only shows web pages and refuses permissions.

features.title: Setup wizard
features.text: Six steps from requirements to connecting assistants, each locked once confirmed.

features.title: Control center
features.text: Start and stop the broker, watch each bot's masked tab, revoke or stop it all.

features.title: Beyond sign-ins
features.text: Unlock files, email codes via Proton Mail Bridge, home-device actions over ssh.

install.label: From source
install.code:
uv sync
cargo build --release --manifest-path wizard/Cargo.toml
wizard/target/release/passbroker-wizard

apps.installNote: Needs the Proton Pass CLI and a desktop that shows notifications. The AppImage runs on glibc 2.35 or newer and downloads Chromium on first run.

apps.name: scale_tail
apps.tag: A system-tray control centre for the Tailscale CLI.
apps.what: scale_tail sits in your tray and drives the tailscale command for you: connect and disconnect, pick an exit node, browse peers, send files with Taildrop and switch accounts. It shows up as a StatusNotifierItem, so it works on KDE and on GNOME with AppIndicator.

features.title: Connect in a click
features.text: Connect, disconnect, auto-connect on launch and start on login.

features.title: Exit nodes
features.text: Pick one, clear it, or use the suggested node.

features.title: Peers
features.text: Copy IPs and DNS names, ping, and send files with Taildrop.

features.title: Toggles
features.text: DNS, subnet routes, LAN access, shields up, Tailscale SSH, advertise exit node.

features.title: Accounts
features.text: Switch accounts, with a login prompt when Tailscale needs auth.

features.title: Updates
features.text: Release checker plus zsync update info for Gear Lever and AppImageUpdate.

apps.installNote: Needs tailscale, libnotify, xdg-utils, wl-clipboard or xclip, and zenity for sending files.

apps.name: oysterAV
apps.tag: One calm GUI over ClamAV, rkhunter, Lynis and friends.
apps.what: oysterAV is a security orchestrator, not another engine. oyst-cli owns every security action and the GTK4 / libadwaita app is a thin client on top, so the CLI and GUI never disagree. Privileged multi-step flows ask for admin once per action.

shots.caption: Scan: profiles, paths and pack cards
Quarantine vault with restore and delete

features.title: Orchestrator, not engine
features.text: Wraps ClamAV, rkhunter, Lynis and more instead of reimplementing them.

features.title: CLI owns security
features.text: oyst-cli is the source of truth. The GUI only talks to it.

features.title: Full or Lite runtime
features.text: Vendored tools under XDG, or host packages only.

features.title: One prompt per action
features.text: Privilege Concert batches multi-step admin work behind one auth.

features.title: Shield
features.text: Firewall, fail2ban and ban management.

features.title: Reports & quarantine
features.text: History, export, resolve; vault with restore and delete.

install.label: CLI
install.code:
uv sync --extra all
uv run oyst-cli setup run --confirm --json
uv run oyst-cli scan ~/Downloads --json

install.label: GUI
install.code:
uv sync --extra gui --extra dev
uv run oysterav

apps.installNote: Needs Python 3.12+ and uv. The GUI also needs system GTK4 and libadwaita. First setup can take a few minutes while signatures download.

apps.name: emobie
apps.tag: A compact emoji palette for content creators. Summon, search, copy, done.
apps.what: emobie puts the full Unicode emoji set behind a global hotkey and a tray icon. Favourites, recents, text macros and as-you-type expansion make it a small writing tool as much as a picker.

features.title: Full catalog
features.text: Every Unicode emoji via emojibase; search by name, tag or shortcode.

features.title: Summon anywhere
features.text: Global hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+Space) and system tray.

features.title: Macros
features.text: Trigger → expansion cards, per-macro hotkeys, YAML import/export.

features.title: Expand as you type
features.text: Opt-in: type a trigger anywhere to replace it.

features.title: Pin on top
features.text: Always-on-top on X11, Plasma Wayland and GNOME Wayland.

features.title: Self-updating
features.text: Optional check that installs the matching release asset.

install.label: Flatpak
install.code:
flatpak install --user emobie-*-x86_64.flatpak
flatpak run io.github.asafelobotomy.emobie

apps.name: hauler
apps.tag: Fast, resumable downloads over parallel connections. Linux first.
apps.what: hauler splits each file across many connections and rebalances them as they finish: when a connection runs out of work, it takes the upper half of whichever segment has the most left. Progress is synced every two seconds, so a crash or reboot resumes where it stopped.

features.title: Dynamic splitting
features.text: Idle connections steal half of the largest remaining segment.

features.title: Crash-safe resume
features.text: One preallocated .part file plus an atomic progress file.

features.title: Safe resume
features.text: If-Range on every request; a changed file restarts instead of mixing versions.

features.title: Live speed limits
features.text: Per-download and global token buckets, adjustable while running.

features.title: Daemon & queue
features.text: haulerd with JSON-RPC over a user socket, SQLite queue, priorities.

features.title: Plays nice with Linux
features.text: Plasma job tracker, logind sleep inhibitor, NetworkManager metered pause.

apps.installNote: The desktop app needs Qt 6, Kirigami, KItemModels and qqc2-desktop-style. On Arch and Manjaro these come with Plasma.

apps.name: ReShadeLinux
apps.tag: Install the official ReShade runtime for Wine and Proton games.
apps.what: ReShadeLinux finds your Steam games, picks the right ReShade hook DLL by reading each executable's imports, and keeps per-game shader choices. ReShade itself is by crosire and its contributors; this project continues kevinlekiller's reshade-steam-proton installer flow.

features.title: Steam detection
features.text: Scans every Steam library and reads appinfo.vdf for the real launch executable.

features.title: DLL selection
features.text: PE import analysis picks dxgi, d3d9, opengl32, ddraw or dinput8.

features.title: Per-game state
features.text: Remembers DLL, architecture, path and shaders per game.

features.title: GUI or CLI
features.text: yad dialogs, falling back to whiptail, dialog, then plain prompts.

apps.installNote: Needs 7z, git, curl, file and python3 on the host. Install yad for the graphical flow.

apps.name: AV Morning Star
apps.tag: Download video and audio from YouTube, Odysee and 1000+ sites.
apps.what: AV Morning Star wraps yt-dlp in a clean desktop app. Basic mode is one click; Advanced mode adds loudness normalisation, denoising, stabilisation and container choice. YouTube cookies are only read with your consent, and only in memory.

features.title: Any quality
features.text: Best, 4K down to 360p, plus audio-only in MP3, FLAC, Opus and more.

features.title: Playlists & channels
features.text: Fetch every entry, pick the ones you want.

features.title: Cookieless by default
features.text: Asks before reading a browser's cookies; never writes them to disk.

features.title: Audio cleanup
features.text: EBU R128 loudness, dynamic normalisation, FFT noise reduction.

features.title: Video cleanup
features.text: hqdn3d denoise, deshake stabilisation, unsharp sharpening.

features.title: Filename templates
features.text: Click tags like Title, Uploader and Quality to build names.

apps.name: XZram
apps.tag: Cross-distro swap management: zram, swap files, partitions and sysctl tuning.
apps.what: XZram is CLI-first. Diagnostics run without root; changes are staged and applied atomically, with a snapshot before every apply so you can roll back. A Qt6 GUI and an optional D-Bus daemon sit on top.

features.title: Read-only diagnostics
features.text: status, detect and doctor, no root needed.

features.title: Staged apply
features.text: Changes stage to pending.json; apply runs them atomically.

features.title: zram
features.text: Configures systemd-zram-generator and migrates from zram-tools.

features.title: Swap files
features.text: Create, resize, remove; enforces nodatacow on btrfs.

features.title: Sysctl tuning
features.text: Swappiness, watermark and page-cluster.

features.title: Snapshots
features.text: Automatic backup before every apply, versioned restore.

apps.name: SCDR
apps.tag: Process scheduling and priority daemon for EEVDF and sched_ext kernels.
apps.what: SCDR is a modern successor to system76-scheduler, drawing on ananicy-cpp, GameMode and scx-loader. It boosts the focused app, audio and games, demotes background apps under CPU pressure, and only ever changes values it owns.

features.title: Rules per process
features.text: Match name, exe, cmdline, cgroup, parent or uid; set nice, slice_us, io, oom and uclamp.

features.title: systemd weights
features.text: Sets cpu_weight and io_weight on the app's unit through systemd itself.

features.title: Live roles
features.text: Foreground (KWin, Hyprland, niri, GNOME), PipeWire audio and GameMode games.

features.title: Pressure aware
features.text: Demotes unfocused apps when PSI crosses a threshold.

features.title: sched_ext policy
features.text: Optionally picks a sched_ext scheduler.

features.title: Polite
features.text: Leaves alone anything rtkit, GameMode, renice or chrt changed.

install.label: Arch (AUR)
install.code:
# packaging/aur in the repo
makepkg -si
systemctl enable --now scdrd

apps.name: Buckler
apps.tag: Debloat and relaunch your NVIDIA SHIELD TV Pro, safely.
apps.what: Buckler is an ADB command-line tool and a custom HOME launcher for the SHIELD TV Pro. Every change is journaled and reversible, OTA drift is detected, and the box is never left without a home screen. It keeps NVIDIA AI upscaling, Play and Chromecast working.

features.title: Probe & audit
features.text: Identity, HOME owner, package state, AI upscaling health.

features.title: Profiles
features.text: Journaled disable-user profiles: privacy-core, speech, minimal, extras.

features.title: buckler-home
features.text: A clean launcher, installed and handed HOME only after it verifies.

features.title: After OTAs
features.text: check --fix re-applies what an update turned back on.

features.title: Tidy
features.text: Find unused apps, clear caches, install open icon packs.

install.label: On the TV
install.code:
# See docs/install.md: install with Downloader on the TV,
# or from a computer over ADB

install.label: Typical flow
install.code:
buckler probe
buckler apply --profile privacy-core
buckler launcher install
buckler launcher handover

apps.name: readit
apps.tag: Profile-first extension for New Reddit: for readers, creators and moderators.
apps.what: readit reshapes New Reddit around who you are rather than restoring Old Reddit. Pick a profile and it sets layout, density and tools to match. A clean-room build, inspired by RedditEnhancer and Moderator Toolbox workflows.

features.title: Focus Reader
features.text: Calm reading layout.

features.title: Dense Power
features.text: More posts per screen for readers and creators.

features.title: Creator Desk
features.text: Tools for posting.

features.title: Minimal Media
features.text: Media-first, chrome-light.

features.title: Mod Desk
features.text: Moderator workflows.

install.label: Chrome
install.code:
npm install && npm run build
# chrome://extensions → Developer mode → Load unpacked → dist/chrome-mv3

install.label: Firefox
install.code:
npm run build:firefox
# about:debugging → Load Temporary Add-on → dist/firefox-mv3/manifest.json

apps.installNote: Store listings would remove the build step for most people; see suggestions below.

apps.name: qbit Plugin Manager
apps.tag: Pick and install qBittorrent search plugins from allowlisted catalogs.
apps.what: Merges the unofficial wiki list, the official nova3 engines and LightDestory's catalog, filters by category and installs straight into qBittorrent's engines folder. Discouraged entries stay unchecked and every plugin gets a static safety check first.

features.title: Multi-source
features.text: Wiki, official nova3 and LightDestory, cached for 6 hours.

features.title: Category filters
features.text: Anime, books, games, movies, music, software, TV and more.

features.title: Safer defaults
features.text: Static review, optional ClamAV scan, discouraged entries unchecked.

features.title: Finds qBittorrent
features.text: Flatpak and native engine folders detected automatically.

apps.name: SonicSound
apps.tag: Album-centred music client for Navidrome, Airsonic and other Subsonic servers.
apps.what: A maintained, modernised fork of SonicLair. Browse by artist and album, play whole albums, radio from similar songs, lyrics when your server has them, and an Android TV build you can drive from your phone.

features.title: Album-centred
features.text: Browse by artist and album; play whole records.

features.title: Android TV
features.text: Leanback UI, phone remote, Jukebox collections, mDNS discovery.

features.title: Radio & lyrics
features.text: Similar-song radio and getLyrics support.

features.title: Works with older servers
features.text: Negotiates API versions for older Airsonic / Subsonic.

install.label: Android
install.code: # Download the APK from the latest release
